title: CLO 2026.0 - Rendering
description: CLO version 2026.0 is now officially released — Make it, for real! CLO technical experts provide a detailed explanation of rendering-related feature optimizations: retaining seam line effects on hair materials, preserving texture display on hair materials, displaying 2D measurement dimensions in style rendering, and adding an option for ground shadows to exclude them from reflections.
transcript:
Hello everyone, in version 2026.0, when applying hair or hair materials, the effect of the gap line can be maintained and the sticker remains visible. Previously, these details were often obscured by hair. This update ensures that the seam structure is still visible and the sticker can be perfectly displayed on the hair surface, thereby improving the visual quality and realism of hair-dyed clothing, hair-dyed toys, and homemade fabrics.

Let’s take a look at how it works. When you use the editor’s sewing line tool to select a fabric type and set it as a single or multiple sewing lines of hair-dyed or hair-dyed-only clothing, a new hair-dye reduction option will appear in the property editor. In the thickness section, you can adjust the width from 0 mm to 100 mm. The unit will be set according to the user’s unit system and is used to adjust the area where hair will be removed. The higher the value, the larger the hair-free area. In this example, I will set this value to 2 mm.

By using the gradient setting under the neckline, you can adjust the distance between the hair-dye area and the hair-dye area to a range of 0 to 100. Since the material type of this fabric is hair-dyed, the result will be visible immediately in the 3D window, but you can also check the final result in the rendering window for a higher sense of realism.

In previous CLO versions, the sticker applied to hair-dyed or hair-dyed materials usually caused the hair to overlap and block the sticker, making it invisible in the rendering window. For example, after applying the hair-dyed material, although the 2D window shows an embroidery sticker, it will not appear in the 3D window. If it is a hair-dyed material, it is also invisible in the 3D window.

In the new version, if you use the adjustment sticker tool to select the sticker, you will notice that the hair-dye reduction option has been added to the property editor. When the sticker is applied to hair-dyed clothing, this option will be enabled by default. You can click the button to activate or deactivate this option by toggling the checkbox. When hair-dye reduction is used, it appears as if the hair has been trimmed in the sticker area, so the sticker is completely visible in both the 3D window and the rendering window.

Please note that depending on the shape and parameters of the hair, such as length and curve, the hair may still cover the sticker in some areas. Please consider this when using long hair-dyed or long hair-dyed materials. If necessary, adjust the parameters accordingly.

Additionally, if your pattern contains non-transparent areas, hair will be visible through transparent regions. For example, if the center of this sticker is completely transparent, the hair will be visible in that specific area.

With the introduction of this feature in version 2026.0, you can better control the design of hair-dyed materials. Whether it is a clothing accessory, hair-dyed toy, or homemade imitation, while maintaining the seam line and sticker perfectly visible on the hair surface, you can fully control the hair length and variation, thereby improving the quality and accuracy of the design.

In version 2026.0, in addition to showing or hiding specific measurement values, the possibility of displaying measurement points in style picture renderings has been increased. The goal is to obtain more technical and information-rich style picture renderings and accurately display the clothing’s measurement values. Let’s look at an example.

Some measurement points have already been added to this file, which are used to determine the clothing’s measurement size and position. After the style picture is rendered, the line includes the 2D measurement size option. By clicking the eye icon, you can toggle the display or hiding of the 2D measurement size. You will notice that the measurement size of the corresponding measurement point is displayed along with it. If necessary, you can change the line color and its opacity. This option applies to the visualization of all measurement points in the project. However, if you need to hide any of them, you can use the measurement point table. You will find the same eye icon next to each measurement point. Simply click the eye icon for the measurement point you want to hide to achieve a clearer and more rational style picture rendering.

By using version 2026.0, your style picture renderings are more accurate and reasonable than ever before. Now let’s start completely controlling your measurement point visibility and simplify your technical package.

In previous CLO versions, when rendering reflective materials—such as metal and glass—the use of the ground shadow option caused the ground shadow environment to appear reflected on the object’s surface. In version 2026.0, you can now remove these shadows from reflections while still maintaining the shadow on the ground, resulting in an improved image.

As you can see, this virtual model is made of glass and has a mirror effect that creates reflective light on a metal layer. Additionally, the attached metal material on the case also reflects light. In the light attributes of the rendering window, using the ground shadow option applies the shadow on the floor. However, because this shadow includes an environmental reflection on its surface, this causes the environment to be visible in the reflection on the virtual model and object.

Starting with this version, a non-reflective option for the ground shadow has been added at the bottom. When you activate this option by selecting the frame, you need to press the synchronize rendering button to apply the change. You will notice that the ground shadow environment no longer appears in the glass and metal materials, and the reflections are no longer present on the glass and metal materials.

Now, by using the new function in CLO 2026.0 that excludes the ground shadow from reflections, you can achieve surprisingly clear reflections without unnecessary shadows, thus further enhancing your rendering experience.

chunks.content: ## Hair-Dyed Material Rendering Enhancements in CLO 2026.0 This section explains the new hair-dye reduction feature in CLO 2026.0, designed to improve the visibility of seam lines and stickers on hair-dyed clothing and materials. Key terms include "hair-dye reduction," "seam structure," and "sticker visibility." In CLO version 2026.0, applying hair or hair materials now preserves the visibility of gap lines (seam lines) and stickers, which were previously obscured by overlapping hair strands. This update ensures that seam structures remain visible and stickers applied to hair-dyed surfaces display clearly, enhancing the realism of hair-dyed clothing, toys, and homemade fabrics. When using the editor's sewing line tool to select a fabric type and apply single or multiple sewing lines to hair-dyed garments, a new **hair-dye reduction** option appears in the property editor. This option allows users to adjust the width of the hair-free area along the seam line, ranging from 0 mm to 100 mm. The unit system adapts to the user's settings. Increasing this value enlarges the area where hair is removed to prevent overlap. Additionally, under the neckline, a gradient setting allows adjustment of the distance between the hair-dye area and the hair-free area, adjustable from 0 to 100. Changes are visible immediately in the 3D window, with the rendering window providing enhanced realism. Previously, stickers applied to hair-dyed materials were obscured in the 3D and rendering windows, even if visible in the 2D window. In 2026.0, selecting a sticker with the adjustment sticker tool activates the hair-dye reduction option by default in the property editor. This can be toggled on or off. When enabled, the hair appears trimmed within the sticker area, making the sticker fully visible in both 3D and rendered views. **Important caveats:** - Hair parameters such as length and curve may still cause partial hair overlap on stickers, especially with long hair-dyed materials. Adjust these parameters as needed. - Transparent areas in stickers allow hair to show through. For example, a fully transparent center in a sticker will reveal hair beneath. This feature improves design control over hair-dyed materials, enabling precise management of hair length and variation while maintaining seam lines and stickers clearly visible on the hair surface, elevating the quality and accuracy of designs. --- ## Measurement Point Visibility and Style Picture Rendering Improvements This section details the expanded control over measurement point visibility in style picture renderings introduced in CLO 2026.0, enabling more technical and information-rich visuals. Key terms include "measurement points," "style picture rendering," and "2D measurement size." Version 2026.0 enhances style picture renderings by increasing options to show or hide specific measurement values and measurement points, allowing for more detailed and accurate technical images of clothing. Users can add measurement points within project files that define clothing size and position. After rendering a style picture, measurement lines display the **2D measurement size** option. Clicking the eye icon toggles the visibility of the 2D measurement size, displaying the corresponding measurement value next to each point.

chunks.title: CLO 2026.0 - Rendering
chunks.content: Key terms include "measurement points," "style picture rendering," and "2D measurement size." Version 2026.0 enhances style picture renderings by increasing options to show or hide specific measurement values and measurement points, allowing for more detailed and accurate technical images of clothing. Users can add measurement points within project files that define clothing size and position. After rendering a style picture, measurement lines display the **2D measurement size** option. Clicking the eye icon toggles the visibility of the 2D measurement size, displaying the corresponding measurement value next to each point. Users can also customize the line color and opacity for all measurement points globally. To hide specific measurement points, the measurement point table includes individual eye icons next to each point, providing selective visibility control for clearer, more rational style picture renderings. This feature allows complete control over measurement point visibility, simplifying the creation of technical packages with more accurate, information-rich style pictures. --- ## Ground Shadow Reflection Control for Reflective Materials This section covers the new ground shadow reflection exclusion feature in CLO 2026.0, which enhances rendering quality for reflective materials like metal and glass. Key terms include "ground shadow," "reflective materials," "non-reflective option," and "synchronize rendering." In previous CLO versions, enabling ground shadows caused the shadow environment to reflect on the surfaces of reflective materials such as metal and glass, resulting in unwanted environmental reflections within the object’s surface. In CLO 2026.0, a **non-reflective option** has been added to the ground shadow settings. When activated, this option removes the ground shadow environment from reflections on glass and metal materials while maintaining the shadow on the ground itself. To apply this feature: 1. Activate the non-reflective option by selecting the frame at the bottom of the ground shadow settings. 2. Press the **synchronize rendering** button to update the scene. After synchronization, the ground shadow no longer appears in reflections on glass and metal surfaces, eliminating unwanted environmental reflections. This results in clearer, more realistic reflections and an overall improved rendering experience for virtual models made from reflective materials. --- # Summary CLO 2026.0 introduces significant rendering enhancements focused on hair-dyed materials, measurement point visualization, and reflection control on reflective surfaces. The hair-dye reduction feature preserves seam lines and sticker visibility on hair-dyed garments. Measurement point controls provide detailed, customizable technical renderings. The new non-reflective ground shadow option improves the realism of reflections on glass and metal materials. Together, these features improve visual quality, precision, and user control in garment design and rendering workflows.
